landmarks.name: Great Pyramid of Khufu
landmarks.blurb: Built c. 2560 BC for Pharaoh Khufu. 2.3 million blocks, originally 146.6 m tall — the tallest human structure for ~3,800 years.

landmarks.name: Queen's Chamber
landmarks.blurb: Queen's Chamber — limestone with a gabled roof, 5.23 x 5.74 m. A niche in the east wall and two narrow "air shafts" lead from it.

landmarks.name: Subterranean Chamber
landmarks.blurb: Subterranean Chamber — cut roughly into the bedrock ~30 m below the base and left unfinished.

landmarks.name: Pyramid of Khafre
landmarks.blurb: Built c. 2570 BC for Khafre. Appears taller than Khufu's pyramid only because it stands on higher bedrock. Keeps its original Tura limestone casing near the summit.

landmarks.name: Pyramid of Khafre — Burial Chamber
landmarks.blurb: Pyramid of Khafre: descending passage to a granite-lined burial chamber containing the royal sarcophagus.

landmarks.name: Pyramid of Menkaure
landmarks.blurb: Built c. 2510 BC for Menkaure, the smallest of the three. Its lowest courses were clad in red Aswan granite.

landmarks.name: The Great Sphinx
landmarks.blurb: A 73 m limestone sphinx with the body of a lion and a royal human head, generally attributed to the reign of Khafre.

landmarks.name: Sphinx Temple
landmarks.blurb: Built of blocks quarried from around the Sphinx itself — an open court ringed by granite-cased pillars, aligned with the equinox sunrise.

landmarks.name: Khafre Valley Temple
landmarks.blurb: Khafre's granite-clad valley temple beside the Sphinx, at the foot of his causeway — its pillared hall held his great seated statues.

landmarks.name: Temple of Amenhotep II
landmarks.blurb: A mud-brick chapel built ~1,100 years after the pyramids by Amenhotep II, who worshipped the Sphinx as Horemakhet, "Horus in the Horizon".

landmarks.name: Khufu Mortuary Temple
landmarks.blurb: Only the black basalt pavement of Khufu's mortuary temple survives — its limestone walls were carried off as building stone.

landmarks.name: Khafre Mortuary Temple
landmarks.blurb: The most complete Old Kingdom mortuary temple: entrance hall, pillared court and five statue niches, built of colossal local limestone blocks.

landmarks.name: Menkaure Valley Temple
landmarks.blurb: Menkaure's valley temple at the foot of his causeway — begun in stone and finished in mud brick after his death.

landmarks.name: Khufu Valley Temple
landmarks.blurb: Khufu's valley temple at the east end of his causeway — its remains lie buried beneath the modern village of Nazlet el-Samman.

landmarks.name: Central Field Quarry (GIS)
landmarks.blurb: The main quarry south of the Great Pyramid, where workers cut the core limestone blocks — leaving stepped benches in the bedrock.

landmarks.name: Menkaure Quarry
landmarks.blurb: Quarry faces and channels south-east of Menkaure — the source of his core blocks, still showing the trenches where stones were levered free.

landmarks.name: Tomb of Khentkaus I
landmarks.blurb: The "Fourth Pyramid of Giza" — the two-tiered rock-cut tomb of Queen Khentkaus I, at the head of the Central Field.

landmarks.name: Workers' Town (Heit el-Ghurab)
landmarks.blurb: Heit el-Ghurab, the "Lost City of the Pyramids": barracks, bakeries and long galleries that housed the crews who built Giza.

landmarks.name: Wall of the Crow
landmarks.blurb: A massive limestone wall (~200 m long, ~10 m high) with a monumental gateway between the plateau and the workers' town.

landmarks.name: Khufu Satellite Pyramid (G1-d)
landmarks.blurb: A small satellite (cult) pyramid for the king's ka.

landmarks.name: Khafre Satellite Pyramid (G II-a)
landmarks.blurb: A small satellite (cult) pyramid for the king's ka.

landmarks.name: Khufu's Solar Boat
landmarks.blurb: A nod to the 43 m cedar "solar barque" found dismantled in a sealed pit beside the Great Pyramid in 1954 and painstakingly reassembled.

landmarks.name: Trial Passages
landmarks.blurb: Rock-cut passages east of the Great Pyramid that reproduce its internal corridors at near-full scale — likely a builders' mock-up.

landmarks.name: Khentkaus Town
landmarks.blurb: A settlement of priests who served the cult of Queen Khentkaus I, built against her monument.

landmarks.name: Workers' Cemetery
landmarks.blurb: Tombs of the pyramid builders on the slope above their town — small mud-brick and stone tombs, some with miniature vaulted superstructures.
